deliverables: WP1: Plutarch and Ply Maintenance, Compatibility & Developer Experience
Critical breakages and serious vulnerabilities response
Bug fixes, correctness improvements, and optimizations
Documentation, examples, technical blog posts, and developer-experience improvements
request.recipient: Intersect 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address for administration on behalf of MLabs/vendor
request.what: Annual funding for maintenance and enhancement of Plutarch and Ply, including compatibility, bug fixes, optimizations, documentation, examples, technical blog posts, and developer-experience improvements.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,162,746 ada, consisting of 1,128,880 ada for Plutarch and Ply maintenance and 33,866 ada for an Intersect budget administration fee.

Plutarch is described as a Haskell eDSL for creating efficient Cardano smart contracts through controlled compilation into UPLC, and Ply is described as tooling for serializing Plutarch scripts to and from CIP-57 blueprint-style artifacts with inferred types.
MLabs says a recent internal audit counted at least 26 teams using Plutarch and Ply, while the rationale separately says the count was at least 15 teams.
The proposal claims Plutarch scripts rank among the smallest in MLabs public cross-language benchmarks while requiring comparatively low on-chain compute and memory.

The proposal says the next funding period is expected to cover Cardano ledger, Plutus, and tooling evolution, including possible Dijkstra-era compatibility if relevant changes land during the funding period.

The proposal claims it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain submission under the approved budget process framework.
The proposal claims the requested amount did not, at submission time, breach the applicable 350M ada Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713, either alone or in aggregate.

The document states MLabs previously received Project Catalyst and Intersect funding for Plutarch/Ply and related tooling, including Fund9 USD 73,040, Fund13 ADA 487,679, Fund13 ADA 57,370, and Intersect ADA 70,000 for Conway-era Plutarch updates.

The proposal says treasury funds will be administered through Intersect using Sundae Labs smart contracts with TRSC and PSSC addresses, external oversight entities, multi-party authorization rules, milestone-based disbursement controls, and a public dashboard.
The proposal claims maintaining Plutarch and Ply will reduce migration risk and support Cardano developer experience, high-value verticals, and open-source smart contract tooling.

summary: The document requests 1,162,746 ada for annual MLabs maintenance and enhancement of Plutarch and Ply, administered by Intersect through treasury smart contracts, with several checkable governance and funding references but limited budget, feasibility, risk, alternatives, and failure-mode detail in the anchor itself.
